summary: The first game against a person: Opus 5 low over the pianist hands on Quicksilver, Armada against an Armada Pawn opening, with a second person advising in chat. Our 0:11 packet put constructors first (Maces and Pawns later) and sent the field builders to the southern spots; the lab queued three constructors in six seconds, the commander built five windmills after the lab (energy 0 at 1:00) and walked to spot_21, and the player, woken by its own echoed 'gl hf', turned chat wakes off and slept 0:19 to 2:09 through the opponent's '~30 pawns before mace' (0:51). His Pawns reached our field constructors at 2:07 against zero soldiers, killed all four constructors by 2:45 and six extractors by 3:48 (480 lost against 54 in the first fight). The home turret and the commander won one trade (3:00-3:18, six Pawns for two windmills), but the player switched the lab to Maces at 3:00, the lab's queue lag turned later orders into three constructors, the hands sent pairs against parties of five to eight four times, and the lab died at 4:43. At least 33 of his Pawns were seen (23 killed, 10 standing at 5:30) when the user ended the game.

summary: A realtime 1v1 in the user's lobby: our Cortex seat (Opus 5 low, Jev 1.13) opened on Matt's line to the lab (lab 0:36, one constructor under corck:1, a Grunt every 9 s from 1:20, ten by 2:43) against an unnamed Armada player's Pawn rush, first seen at D4 at 2:03. After the lab the commander was told to help it instead of building Matt's generator batch, so the energy store sat at zero from 1:16 to 2:06 with about 450 metal banked. At first contact the hands split our Grunts into pairs and singles, a pair chased one Pawn 2,700 out to G6, and his party, grown to 6-9 Pawns, met our soldiers piecemeal at E3/D4 while the commander built windmills 550 away with no attack row on its menu: eight Grunts died by 3:14 for four Pawns. The constructor and two extractors fell 2:38-3:19, the switch to Thugs (first out at 3:15) emptied the energy again, and the commander's first fight, alone at the lab from 3:26, ended in its death at 3:31, the blast levelling the lab. The user: 'it let pawns drift too far out and didn't use its commander to improve exchange rates early on'; the groups and the commander's row were fixed that night (e5600f0).

Our two seats met his party one group at a time and lost nearly every fight with more metal on the spot, except at 8:03-9:13 (lost 1,694, killed 1,975); after that the west group flipped thirty times between a station under his turrets and home. Under all of it was a seat fault fixed the same day: the first turn saw one seat, and one name space for two seats sent the lists and standing orders to whichever seat ticked first. So no list step played before 3:00, no scout was ever made, and the never list and the stations landed on the wrong seat. He came west at 13:25 with Warriors, then a Fatboy (seen 14:14) and Zeus (14:38); the west commander died at 14:20, the east at 15:28. We lost 25.5k and saw 4.4k of his die.

No list step played on either seat before 3:00: both plants defaulted to bot labs, the scout cars were never made, and his base was never seen. The same drain later split the standing orders across seats. The cost began at 4:26, when his commander walked into groups that met it one at a time.

summary: Single Rovers and Blitzes took our naked outer spots from 2:31, the middle seat falling to 2 extractors at 4:00, while our three starved openings had 6-10 factory units by 4:00 against the pool's 17-19. From 4:00 to 13:00 our three seats' army was at least 4 times what we saw of his, and we held up to 29-31 extractors. But at 4:30 the player split it into two home pickets and a lone north raid, which stalled at C1 and lost 11 for 2 at 7:51. The first combined push, 64 Blitzes of two seats at 9:30, traded 7,040 for 4,825 into his D3/C3 nest of beamers, light turrets and Stouts, and his factory was never seen. The middle seat's ball of 44-53 Blitzes, the home guard by the player's word and beyond every later tool order because of the standing drain, held at H5 while one block of 8-10 Stouts and 4-7 Janus, seen at 11:30, killed the north seat (commander_t1 at 14:24). The ball then won every fight it joined (his 22 Stouts and 5 Janus lost 6,150 at G4, 15:10-16:09), but six Stouts took the south plant at 16:37, and Thunders (17:48) and Banshees (19:28) met no anti-air; the middle seat fell at 19:51 and the south at 21:21.

lens.caveats: There is no truth file, results.jsonl or batch.json, so his numbers are floors of what we saw. Where I differ from review.md: (1) it ranks the H5 hold first (decided by 14:00, cost-ranked), while cause before symptom puts the root at the 4:30 split; (2) its finding 5 makes the third seat's absence at 9:30 the player's, but the 9:07 transcript ordered group_B_t3 a southern prong (station spot_61) that the drain ate; (3) the ball's first move was the hands' 13:01 [plan] attack, when the block reached F3 (a spot in the 12:31 packet's trigger list); the 13:32 packet played at 13:43, not 13:33; and the ball was still at G3 (6,364, 1,828) at 14:23, not at G2 at about 14:20. I removed mine and pointed their strategist-0.jsonl and bot.log links at their match; that reader's per-seat runs at about 00:17 may have read this match.

summary: Three Opus-run seats (t1 Armada at G1, t2 and t3 Cortex at H8 and G4) against thebluegecko on Comet, with Irishstud14 spectating and advising in chat. The Cortex seats' opening lists were all refused (the tools knew the lead seat's Armada roster only), yet the side held 34 extractors at income 102 by 10:45, and t2+t3's Thug ball broke his D3/D4 outpost by 10:18 while the packet kept t1's ground army at home at F2; from 11:05 the ball met his Stout-and-Janus blocks one group at a time at C3, D4 and E4. Counting each death once, the trade was even to 14:00 (12.8k lost to 13.1k destroyed), but the player's report summed the three seats and read about 3:1 in our favour all game. From 14:14 his Banshees (no anti-air of ours until 15:13), then Mausers firing from out of sight (16:23) and Bulls (18:21) beat a tier-1 army that never went tier 2 and never saw his base; our commanders died at 22:12 and 24:08, and t1's self-destructed at about 26:13 when a spectator suggested it. Irishstud14 at 15:06: "red not moblizing fast enough is what lost you the game".

The person (Irishstud14) gives the same cause; red = t1 is our reading.

summary: Irishstud14 declared 'I greed then' (0:27) and took naked extractors behind Rascal raids, while our three seats opened slowly (3-4 solars before the plant, 7-9 factory units by 4:00 against the pool's p25 of 16-17) and kept their first soldiers as pickets on our strip, the constructors fenced out of his half and the commanders out of the middle. thebluegecko, spectating, called it from 3:58 to 5:53 ('almost caught up to the three claude players by building naked mexes', 'an aggressive response is needed'); our raiders first crossed at 6:32-7:20 and the north and middle groups pushed his main base at B3 on hold-line, where Pounders from 8:10 broke the Blitzes (about 25 lost on seat 0, 11 of them on a retreat through the Pounder line at 9:02-9:19). The middle game was even: Lashers, then Brutes and Pounders on his advice, and a 9k three-group strike on his commander at D3 (11:59-13:27) that killed his escort but let him walk away. From 13:22 swarms of 10-18 Incisors slipped past the slower Brute ball and took our extractors from 31 to 11 by 17:00, his Graverobbers raised our Stouts from the unreclaimed E3 wreck field from 17:28, the army collapsed at F3 (17:37-18:18) and two commanders died by 20:05. Counted once per death across the three records, the fights were about even (our army lost 37.8k against his 42.4k seen) and the whole trade was lost (62.4k against 44.7k): one person out-produced three seats, as thebluegecko put it at 18:57, 'irish expanded faster than the three claude bots, even fight on first contact'.

root.what: Against an opponent who had announced a greedy opening, the player turned the first soldiers of every seat into pickets on our own extractors (stations from 2:07 and 2:58), barred the commanders from the middle columns (3:13) and the constructors from 32 spots of his half (4:10), on top of a metal-starved opening whose plants 'idle on metal' (its own 3:13 note). So the first window, 2.3-6.9x his seen army on every seat at 4:00-5:00, was spent at home while he took naked extractors, and our expansion stayed on the strip. The cause is the person's reading (3:58, 4:22, 18:57); the orders behind it are from the transcript.

summary: A 3v1 on Comet Catcher: three seats of ours (two Cortex, one Armada, one Opus 5.5 medium player for all three) against [gecko]Infern8 (Armada, lobby 25), with thebluegecko and Irishstud14 coaching from the spectators' chat. We won when his plant died at 9:29 and his commander at 9:35, both at B4. The opening was slow on every seat: the plant at 0:49 after three solars, scout cars first, commanders off the plant after 25 s, and plants idle in half the samples to 5:07 under a hands default that was fixed during the game. The spectators named each of these faults as it happened. He raided with Blitzes (F6 at 3:35; seat 0's F1/E1 at 4:41-4:55, two extractors) but showed little army. summary: Three Opus-led seats against Infern8 (lobby 25, Cortex) on Comet Catcher, lost at about 17:05 with two commanders dead. The side out-expanded him (30 extractors at 8:00 against 9 ever seen) but kept a mostly light army at home as pickets. It killed one building of his in the game's first 16 minutes, and he walked his commander forward to D4 with a second plant, a light turret, Brutes and, from 8:29, Pounders. The player gathered the three seats for 90 s and ordered one attack at 8:14. Each seat's hands priced its own group alone, so the seats went in one after another and about 80 soldiers (10.2k) fell to 24 for about 3.5k of his. After that, reading a trade line that counted every kill three times, the player held and rebuilt: one good fight at 12:08 (18 Brutes), then his single block of Pounders and Brutes beat dark blue's lone group at 13:04 and took dark blue's home by 14:28 and purple's by 16:18, while up to 14k of wrecks lay unreclaimed and the advanced plant begun at 10:16 never finished; the distinct trade was 24.4k of his for about 50k of ours.

At 8:20, 60 of our 78 armed units were light (31 Incisors, 19 Blitzes, 10 scout cars), and they died into his Pounders and Brutes at D4. The ledger: 'he went Pounders and Brutes early'.
Raiders stood as home pickets. Apart from an extractor at 2:18, nothing of his died before 16:43, and the lone person built a forward plant at D4 unharassed.
The same lesson against another person: our economic lead (30 extractors against 9 seen at 8:00) went unused while his economy and forward plant were never raided.
'I would go around rather than attack the strongest position.' The attack went head-on into his commander, light turret and Pounders at D4, for 9.6k lost against 3.5k.

Infern8, this game's opponent, said the next day that defences are strong per metal and need range or overwhelming force. Here his LLT and commander at D4 anchored a block that light raiders could not break.
This is a rematch of game 5, which was won by converging on him. Here the lead (9.3k of soldiers at 8:00, all at F4) was held at home until 8:24 and then spent on the strongest point.
From 10:00, 3.5k to 12k of wrecks lay in our half with 0 constructors at work. His Graverobbers raised them at F5/F6 from 15:02.
No seat built a construction turret all game. Purple's advanced plant, started at 10:16, was still unfinished when it died at 16:05.
The advanced plant came late (started at 10:16, the first of the six games per the ledger) and never finished. His Reapers were in sight at 17:00.
The player made his commander the target (6:45-8:14). The words had no rule to land in, and the commander lived.

At 7:00 his Blitz army was spent (the player's note: ~40 killed, his commander at B4 with 3 constructors), and the player ordered group_A_t1 and group_A_t2 to advance 'together' and attack_unit the commander. His commander D-gunned 11 of the 16 Incisors lost, and the fall-back at 7:58 walked the rest 3,845 back to F2. The next attack that arrived together (sent 13:00) killed him within a minute. Our reading; thebluegecko named the stall at 7:26.

Incisors that came at his commander one by one lost 16 (11 to the D-gun) at 7:49-8:11; three groups together killed it at 13:59, though 13 Brutes died in its death blast.
From 7:00 his army in sight was near zero against 5.8k. The three-minute hold (7:57-10:47) let him rebuild with Stouts and Janus, and the close came only at 13:59.

Purple's advanced plant drew from a store at 0-69 beside two tier-1 plants still producing; it never finished, and the game was won on tier 1.
Our player announced its state and plans in chat ('23 extractors, 11 constructors' 5:09; 'Sending our 22-Incisor group south' 8:53). Whether the opponent could read it is unknown.

bears_on.note: This game is the lesson's first case. Asked about the Bull switch, he answered that the game was over by 15:00 on metal. The trade counted once (behind in every phase but one) and 24 Bulls from 14:54 agree with him.
We held about half the map (44 of 80 spots at 10:35) and stopped, with the constructors barred from his half. Against him, half was not enough.

The seen lead at 7:10 and 13:24 was never converted, against game 5's converge-and-kill. Note that the lead was partly a floor of sight: his seen army was small, and the trade counted once ran against us.
The player's own notes: 14:13 'the spot_59 push arrived piecemeal'; 15:42 '3 Bulls beat our Stouts in ones'.
Nothing was reclaimed; 9.7k to 15.5k of wrecks were offered late, and 29k of ours died west of the middle, where he could eat it.
His Bulls beat a tier-1 army of Stouts, Janus and Pounders; our own tier 2 stood only at 16:12.
Pounders used as the offensive ball against Bulls lost 34 for 195 metal.

The scout cars crossed at 2:20 and saw his commander at B5, but the first raider mass crossed only at 5:43. The first building of his to die was a light turret at D5 (6:07, the map's middle); the first in his own corner was at B1 at 7:37.

lens.caveats: There is no truth file, so his army, extractors and income are floors from our sight. The case that his economy outgrew three seats rests on the person's word and on 24 distinct Bulls seen, not on a measured income. minutes, analyze_match, floor, raid_ledger and hands_window read only record-0 (t1), so t2 and t3 were run through scratch directories linking record-N as record-0. pro_baseline compares single seats with a 1v1 pool: t1 (G1 Cortex) is uncarded, t2 needs --all-starts, and its pressure rows are blank without a truth start. The match directory holds no review.md, but it has posing-review.md and decompression-review.md (2026-09-27), and this row builds on both. Where it differs: the posing review's estimate of 'at least 46 metal a second' used the seat-summed 37,188; counted once, it is 12,396. The chat lines' speaker is '?' in chat.jsonl and 'player 0' (the opponent's seat) in bot.log; the attribution to thebluegecko is the record header's, the ledger's and L-mex-game-over's. The event def ids are offset by one from the header's unit_defs ids, and the reader's script corrected for this. impedance_sweep counts one session replacement. The loss does not rest on a since-fixed defect alone: the Bull phase leaned on the reach-less odds, and the player's belief that it was ahead leaned on the triple-counted trade, but the person put the decision on metal before 15:00.

our_side: Three seats of ours on the east edge, all Armada (the lobby side was 'random'): t1 orange at H6 (record-0), t2 sky blue at H4 (record-1), t3 green at H2 (record-2). One player, claude-opus-5-5 at effort medium (Claude Code 2.1.283), over all three seats, with no commander role. The hands were Jev jev-1.13.0, and the decompression stage was on. summary: thebluegecko opened as greedily as a person can: two Pawns were his only army until his first Welder at 7:41, he reclaimed his bot lab at 5:12 and both shipyards for an advanced bot lab at 6:58, and his construction ships took the sea (16 extractors under water by 8:00, 24 by 10:00). We took none of the map's 26 underwater spots, because every Beaver step to one was skipped as 'not free' and every shipyard order snapped to land; both were picture defects, fixed the next day in b9a43ff. Our three seats' combined army was 3.0k, 6.9k and 11.7k against his 108, 108 and 1,158 at 4, 6 and 8 minutes, but all three Rovers turned home at 2:41-2:53 and the player held and then gathered the groups in our half (3:56-7:57) instead of crossing. The commit reached his base strung out at 8:35, met five Welders, two Beamers and an LLT, and lost 6.7k while killing two Welders (700). From then on his sea extractors and reclaim-fed income outgrew us (40 extractors to our 29 at 10:00), and our Stouts broke Welder pushes at spot_29 but lost every advance through the E3 neck. His army grew from 4.3k at 10:00 to 18.5k at 16:00, and Liches from air plants we never saw killed all three commanders at 17:19, 17:29 and 18:18.

root.what: At 3:56 the player read 'army 2.7k vs 54 seen' and ordered the three groups to stand together at the D2 choke and hold, advancing only once they had gathered. His base had been unseen since 2:41-2:53, when the hands' pick sent each seat's Rover home on sighting a constructor and a Pawn about 700 from his start. His whole army until 7:41 was two Pawns, an LLT, a commander and one or two Beamers, and from 5:12 to 7:22 he had no land factory. The window was 3:00-8:00, at 3.6-35x on seat 0 alone. It was spent in our half: the gather stalled, and the commit landed after his Welders. Everything after 8:35 is its cost.

lens.caveats: The match has no truth file. The re-simulated replay /ceph/christian/within-reason/run/matches-archive/1790483222-replay-human-cape-violet supplies truth-1..3 with the live game's unit ids (our commander is 11775 in both), so his numbers are true, not floors. The per-match tools read record-0 only, so seats 1-2 were read through scratchpad directories of symlinks. On truth, analyze_match counts his reclaimed buildings (armlab 5:12, armsy 6:50, 7:42) as losses. The sea count maps each extractor to its nearest spot (it reads 27 for 26 at 14:00). The 273 income at 10:00 is the card's figure, with reclaim not separated. chat.jsonl marks all four comments '?'; bot.log gives player 3 (the host's seat) without the [WReason] prefix, which design §6 rules are the user's. pro_baseline was not run (Comet only), nor was impedance_sweep. That a push at 4:00-6:00 would have won is my reading; his commander and D-gun are unpriced. Where I differ from the model reviews and the ledger: (1) posing-review ranks by cost (21.8k to Welders first); this row ranks by root, the 3:00-8:00 window against a factory-less opponent, which those reviews could not see without a truth file. (2) The B3 push killed 700 (two Welders), not 2.1k. (3) Liches killed three commanders (17:19, 17:29, 18:18), not two. The ledger's and the reviews' other findings stand.

summary: Our three seats led on every count we could see from 4:00 to 12:00: 2.2k to 17.3k of army against at most 900 of his in sight, and 34 extractors at 7:00. The lobby's start boxes were not honoured, so the rovers and the picture looked for him in the top rows (which hold our own G1 seat), the player read the empty north as a base in the north-west (B1-C2, marked 5:24), and no unit of ours ever entered A4-C8, where his raids came from. bears_on.note: This game is the lesson's source. 59 Lashers and 2 Brutes were made from 13:00 to 18:00 with the army held at D2 ('They do NOT go west', 13:16). His first Tiger came at 17:46, and the tier 2 killed 57 Lashers in two fights (18:43-20:01).

'Pounders for defence': 6 Pounders, 3 Brutes and drones held B3 against 21 Brutes and 17 Stouts (12:26-13:36, about 9.5k of ours for 3.5k). Our answer, Lashers to outrange Pounders, loses the sim duel to Pounders (-0.72) and Brutes (-0.65).
We held 5-20x his seen army from 4:00 to 12:00 (12.0k at 10:00 against 560 seen) and never reached his base. The lead was spent in columns E-G and on the empty north row.
The B3 push was two of three groups, already worn (Brutes at 80%). t3's 16 Brutes stayed at F5, and the Stouts lost 7 more at 13:19-13:36 after the Brutes were gone.
The 0:00 packet: 'the rest hold at home'. No soldier of ours went near his real side, A4-C8, all game, while his Rascals were at our G5 by 2:41.

Build power, not metal, bound the top seat's tier 2 after 17:31: about one constructor on the coravp (20-24% a minute) while the store rose to 1,153-1,432. In the user's words, gifted metal is nothing without the build power (3086b7c).

The user's 17:27 comment says the same thing (stop the other lab during the transition), and the player paused plant_8535 at 17:31. Stopping production alone did not speed the plant, since the helpers' assist steps were dropped. The bottleneck was build power.

The relay was said after this game. In the records, the top seat's commander assisted 67 s of the first 4:00 (assist4; pool 50), often from the plant's exit lane (wakes 1:45-4:17). The plant stalled on metal, not build power: stall4 65%, store 2 at 3:00 and 4:00, 11 factory units by 4:00 against the pool's p25 of 16.

We never held or visited anything west of column D below row 2 (A4-C8, D7, D8). His outposts sat at E3/E4/D5/E6 and his extractors in our south-west. Our extractors fell from 34 at 8:00 to 26 at 9:00, peaked at 39 at 18:00, and 72 were lost over the three seats.

His Twin Guard (corhllt) nests at E3/E4 (6:25-7:54), C1 (7:40), D5 (11:25) and E6 (16:06) held the middle. The player kept constructors and groups off them with 'never' lists and cleared them only with the whole ball (8:31, 10:49-11:30).
Exit lanes were blocked by our commanders and builders all game (12 lane wakes). The player's 25:00 note: 'the packet could not move them'.

lens.caveats: No truth file, batch.json or results.jsonl, so his economy, army and base location are unknown and his numbers are floors. minutes.py, analyze_match, floor, raid_ledger, wake_read and hands_window read only record-0 (the top seat); seats 1 and 2 were read through private symlink directories. My first try put those links in the shared scratchpad's seat1/seat2, which belonged to another reader, so the tools read the SD-129 game. Those numbers were thrown away and the other reader's links restored. pro_baseline needs --all-starts, and then it compares one seat of a 3v1 to a duel pool. The date: the batch's unix time reads 2026-09-27 16:54 UTC, but lessons.md, the inbox file and the commit messages date game 10 2026-09-28 (the machine clock ran a day behind the session's dates). chat.jsonl marks the 17:27 line '?'. The record gives it to player 2, the host's seat, without the [WReason] prefix, and the rework design (section 6) makes that the user's comment. The inbox file players-chat-2026-09-28.md gives it to thebluegecko and review.md to a spectator. Where I differ from review.md: (1) The tier-2 plant was not at 0% for three minutes. The 15:40 frame built 7/27/47/71% at 16-19:00 and stood at 19:43. The 0% frame was a second one, started by the player's 18:00 'coravp spot_5' (placed 18:35, dropped 19:15). The cause was build power: dropped assist steps and about one constructor, as the user said (3086b7c). (2) The B3 push was two groups (19-22 Brutes and 17 Stouts at A2 at 12:26), not the top seat's Brutes alone, and it lost about 9.5k with the Stouts. (3) The 0:00 packet did ask scouts for the west strip, so the rovers' box ranking overrode a correct instruction. (4) My three-seat army counts finished units only (12.0k at 10:00 against the review's 12.7k). The rest of the review stands, ranked here by root.

How big were his economy and army at 8:00-12:00, when we held 9-17k against at most 900 seen? Would the 9k ball sent west along rows 3-5 at 8:31 have found and broken his base before his Pounders and drones massed?
3086b7c fixed the second frame. Was the dropped bare 'assist' step (17:39 'could not be played this second and was dropped') also fixed, by the hands rebuild or later?

The per-match tools read record-0 only; seats 1 and 2 were run through scratchpad symlink directories. minutes.py's 'he starts F6' is the snap bug's guess, which voids its 'his half' columns and the 8:00-11:00 and 13:00-15:00 windows. analyze_match's army column now counts hovers, but its engagement 'on the spot' soldier values are still 0 for them. pro_baseline.py was not run (Comet only). chat.jsonl marks the host lines '?'; they are attributed here to the user (computer_whisperer) by the host-seat rule in design §6 and docs/knowledge/_inbox/players-chat-2026-09-28.md. The date is 2026-09-27 by the batch's epoch and the files; the brief passage and the lessons give 2026-09-28, the relay date. summary: One Opus 5.5 low seat (Armada, south-east) played the user himself (computer_whisperer, Armada, north-west) in realtime on Avalanche 3.4 and lost at about 12:34 when its commander died at home. The pre-game role-word list was in force at 0:02, but the player's 0:10 turn swapped its solars and third extractor for seven wind turbines, and at 1:50, in a wind lull with the energy store empty, listed two more turbines ahead of the first constructor's extractors: ten turbines by 2:20, the energy store full and metal at 0 from 3:00, two extractors from 0:15 to 3:08 and never more than six of our ten spots (income 3.5-11.6). His Pawns were in our half from 2:18; at 4:01-4:10 two parties split our one Pawn group, which switched target four times, and four extractors fell by 5:31 with no raiding party paying. Our one counter-raid (12 Pawns, 6:25) killed his E4 outpost and was walked home by a since-fixed losses-line defect; his factory was never seen. From 8:27 his Maces and Centurions (reach 380 against the Pawns' 180) beat our Pawns at F4/F5, walked into the base at 10:55 while our army was at D6 against his turret creep (1,272 lost for 530), and killed the commander at the lab at 12:23-12:33.

summary: The user played a self-described silly build: constructor aircraft expanding into our half, Banshees from about 4:54, then Centurions from 8:23. lens.caveats: The opponent is a person, so there is no truth file: his army, extractors and tier 2 are only what we saw (floors), and minutes.py's HIS TIER 2 is empty. The archive has no results.jsonl or batch.json, so analyze_match prints outcome None; the result comes from the ledger and bot.log ('enemy base ... is razed' at f=31605). pro_baseline.py was not run: Avalanche is not Comet and has no pool cards. commander_turns --told was not read in full; the instructs were extracted whole from strategist-0.jsonl. That a push from B4 at 8:24 would have won earlier is the reader's reading. The only person's words are the user's two ledger quotes; there are no chat comments. The ledger reads the army as 'held from 0:00 to 13:30'. This reader differs in part: from 6:21 to 8:34 the army did raid his half (67% of our mass there at 8:00, at B4 at 8:24), but his base (spot_1/spot_2) stayed barred until 13:30. summary: A realtime 3v1 on Comet Catcher: one Opus 5.5 player on three Armada seats against thebluegecko (Cortex, B5). It ended at 10:20, when a Stout and Shellshocker push killed his commander at B4; his plant fell at 10:21. Our side out-expanded him from the start (18 extractors at 4:11 and 47 at 9:13, against at most 13 of his seen) and lost only two extractors, both to two Rascals at 2:57 and 3:21. Its army led by 3.5x or more from 4:11 (6.3k against about 0.5k seen at 7:30), but until 7:30 the packet kept it off his plant and commander and sent Blitz groups one at a time to D4 and C4. There his Incisors (17 Blitzes killed, 4:00-7:00) and then Pounders (16 Blitzes and 5 Stouts, 6:00-10:00) won the exchanges, and the seen trade stood at 3,964 lost to 2,941 destroyed at 8:12. The player moved two plants to Stouts at 6:02 and the third at 8:12, sent one heavy body at his plant at 7:30, and the push was fighting at his base from 9:37; his commander killed 16 of ours before it died, and he never showed tier 2 or fought in our half after 3:00.

root.what: Nothing ever put the win at risk; this root marks where the game's cost and length were set (the reader's reading, no person commented). With the side's army at about 3.5x his seen, the packet sent each Blitz group to spot_33 (D4) to join one body that raided outer spots, and repeated that it never goes at his plant or commander (first said at 2:37, again at 6:02). Blitzes walked in a few at a time to his Incisors and then Pounders until the 7:30 push order; that one body ended the game in under three minutes.

their_play: thebluegecko played Cortex from B5, with a single vehicle plant standing at B4 by 2:20 and a construction turret beside it by about 9:00. He raided our south seat early, with two Rascals that killed two fresh extractors at 2:57 and 3:21, and otherwise defended his half with light turrets on his extractors (one killed a Rover at 2:57) and Exploiters on outer spots (by 5:39). His army changed as ours did: Incisors from about 4:00, which killed 17 Blitzes in C4/B3/D4 by 7:00; Pounders from 5:40, which killed 16 Blitzes and 5 Stouts; a Brute by 7:54. He fought only in his own half (his mass C4/B4, 0% in ours after minute 3) and showed no tier 2. At the end his commander fought at the plant and killed 16 of ours before dying at 10:20. His extractors seen never passed 13, against our 47. A 3v1 at even resources with his economy unseen: the reader cannot say how far behind he was, only that he held a negative trade against us until the base fell.

bears_on.note: He brought Pounders in from 5:40, which killed 16 Blitzes and 5 Stouts. Our switch to Stouts (medium tanks), last plant at 8:12, carried the push that killed him. The player's own summary: 'Blitzes lost the trade to Pounders 6:30-8:30'.
Our Blitz mass was answered first by Incisors (17 Blitzes killed) and then by Pounders, while our plants kept making Blitzes.
The side led 3.5x to over 12x in army from 4:11, and the lead went into raids until the 7:30 order to push. One body then went from E3 at 8:46 to his commander's death at 10:20.
Blitz groups reached D4 one at a time from 4:32, and at 7:54-8:04 the hands split three hunts ahead of the body. The trade was negative until the base fell.
The 9:45 order was to attack his commander first when seen, and it died at 10:20, but only after it had killed 16 of ours at its plant.
The first Rovers were in his half at 2:07 and found his base, but killed nothing. The first kills (an extractor, a constructor and an Incisor at B3) came with the Blitzes at 4:19.
The Rovers got within 281 of his start at 2:31 without doing damage (trade 0 destroyed at 3:06), and one died to a light turret at 2:57.
Plants were idle 13-14% of their time on uncounted produce entries, by the player's own note and the records' idle flag.
The side held 47 extractors at 9:13 against at most 13 of his seen and lost only two. The economy carried a negative army trade through to the win.
Wreck fields at C4 and B3 reached 4,259 metal and were never worked, in a game short enough that it did not matter.
Every seat built three solars and then a constructor as the plant's first unit (1:24), as the lesson intends, but the plants stood at 1:23-1:33, past the pool's p75.
There were 8 wakes on blocked plant exit lanes, and t1 lost 430 unit-seconds to stuck units.

summary: This was our second game on Cape Violet: three Cortex seats against thebluegecko. On our side of the map we out-expanded him: 37 extractors by 10:16, 12 of them on under-water spots taken by Muskrats, and none of his extractors was ever seen. By 14:00 the three seats' army was 24.8k against 1.7k of his seen. But all of it went by land into his B3 nest, which sits on the only land passage. Twin Guards repaired by construction turrets, then Sumos and Mammoths, took 5.6k for 0.5k by 10:16 and 16.1k for 3.8k in the three minutes to 17:04. Meanwhile he took the sea and climbed the tech: his torpedo launchers killed 11 of our sea extractors from 11:02 with none answered, a Despot battleship sat in the central lake from 19:56, Shivas came from 18:02, and Wasps and a cruise-missile ship arrived by 25:00. We had no ship, plane or anti-air all game, and his Shivas and Wasps broke the bases at 24:30-26:00. The user's verdict was that the early economic lead was never converted into damage, and that air or naval units were needed early, or siege units used properly.

root.what: The player saw his lab on the B3 passage, the only land way west, and planned to break it by land with tier-1 tanks. The 'shipyard decision at ~2:30' from 0:05 lapsed, although the brief in force said to build a shipyard by 4:00 and never to walk into the B3 camp. From here the leads went into the one place he was strongest, and the sea, his road and his economy, was left to him (person-backed: the user, 25:40).

our_side: Three seats: t1 red Armada F8 (record-0), t2 green Armada H8 (record-1), t3 magenta Cortex C8 (record-2). summary: We out-expanded him early (side 91 extractors at 9:28, 112 at 17:16) and the report showed an army lead of 4-30x over what we saw, but the lead was against a floor: the side never scouted his half, his base was found only at 10:09 (E2) and his units destroyed in our sight already came to 19.7k metal by 16:00 and 74k by 22:00. Our pressure went at his base side (F1/F2) as trickles of Blitzes into Exploiters, Pounders and then Twin Guard nests, while from 9:28 every new group was a home guard, so magenta's army (13.7k-36.6k from 16:00) stood in C6-C8 for 18 minutes. The hands split groups into detachments chasing raiders; his Brute raids took magenta's home from 44 to 16 extractors at 18:36-21:43 while its guard held. He reached tier 2 unseen (Tzar reported 22:02, Tigers 25:49) and raised 138 of our dead with Graverobbers; his Tzar push broke the east seats from 26:44, both Armada commanders died at 29:46 and 30:54, and the engine closed the game at 32:19. The one player's turns slowed from 15.7 s to 30.3 s and its notes named each problem minutes after it began (the ledger's reading).

bears_on.note: The user said at 5:11-5:24 what the lesson says of a greedy expander ('an agressive responce is needed'); our raid hit his defended base side instead of his spread spots and his economy grew unseen to about our size.
We did the 'keep taking mexes' half (112 extractors at 17:16) and not 'raiding the corners'; expansion alone did not hold against an unraided person on a 437-spot map.
The end was the economy: extractors 112 at 17:16, 86 at 20:07, 63 at 27:24, 39 at 29:26, 9 at 31:45, while the trade the player read was even or positive.
The groups never fought as one: red's Blitzes and Stouts fed into F2-F4, green's into G3-F4, magenta's body stayed west; the player's own 16:13 and 27:24 notes say so.

A seen lead of 38.5k against about 5k at 16:13 was never taken into him, but it was against a floor (his destroyed-in-sight 19.7k by then): the lesson needs a lead measured against his estimate, not his sightings.
Blitzes and Stouts sent head-on into Exploiters and Twin Guard nests at F2, F3, F4 (13:40, 15:30, 22:21) bled each time.
'go arround rather than attack the strongest postition': 19 Stouts lost in 27 s at the F3 nest at 23:15.
Blitzes into Pounders and Brutes lost; the player switched to Stouts and Whistlers only at 14:01.
From his side: Graverobbers raised 138 of our dead from the fields our piecemeal attacks left, 89 of them by 25:00.
Stores high with build power missing: magenta's energy empty 42% of the game with 2.7-4.4k metal banked; 6.2k banked at 17:54.

lens.caveats: A game with a person: no truth file, results.jsonl or batch.json, so his side is what we saw (floors), the result is inferred from the last sample, and analyze_match prints 'outcome None after 0.0 min'. minutes.py takes his start as B5 (his base was at A8) and finds no WINDOWS (his army reads 0). pro_baseline has no carded side from G1 ('no carded side ... from ['B8', 'G1']'); I used --all-starts (39 Cortex sides from all starts), whose pressure rows are '-' without his start. known%/look_min not computable. No tool reads commander.jsonl; read directly. A parallel reader overwrote one scratch output of mine (a shared scratch name); I regenerated it before quoting. Where I differ from the existing review: the root framed as the lost pressure (the user's reading), not only the lost scout; the 9:54 Thistle order skipped for want of a place; the solar clause stood 3:33-6:30 (dropped at 6:55), not to 8:20; the exit-lane extractor (since fixed) and the lane rove (since fixed) named; the commander's 9:38 north-west guess noted.

open_questions: When did he start his advanced aircraft plant, and where was his T1 air plant (never seen)? Would a Rascal at A8 at about 4:30 have seen it? (no truth file)
Is the 'join group_B there' -> 'follow group_B' play, which pulled seven units out of his half, possible in today's hands?
Is 'armdrag' credited with kills a disguised Dragon's Claw reported under its disguise, and does the report still name it so?
Why did the engine refuse eight cormex orders as bad sites (F2, F3, G4, F4, E2, E1)? A placement-geometry fault of that build?
Are the commander seat's wakes (first tier-2 aircraft, large losses) and the wake lines' loss counts fixed since 2026-10-04?
What did his "holy crap eco balance" (4:08) and "crap" (5:19) refer to? Nothing in our record explains them.

bears_on.note: Both ways: our extractors without turrets died to single Rovers from 2:34, and his naked greedy expansion lost six extractors and a constructor to three Rovers and one Blitz by 4:59.

Our first handful crossed (Blitz 2:10, his first extractor dead 3:02 against the pool median 2:48) and paid. His handful crossing the other way did the same to us. Scope: the crossing needs a picket at home (a turret) beside it, or it trades evenly.

In part: three of our Rovers on rove, with no special micro, killed six extractors and a constructor against a greedy opener's naked spots. The lesson's 'need specific micro to be worth anything' was said of a Rover mass against a guarded opening.
Extractors decided it: we never held more than 8 (2 at 5:00, 3 at 8:00), against his sighted 9+ at 7:47, 11 at 9:43 and 16 at 13:25; the armies traded about evenly 6:30-9:21.

The commander held the body home 4:47-10:13 on '8 extractors first' with his plant seen unturreted at 4:09, but the army lead was a floor of what was in sight. The commander read 'even, about 1,000 a side' at 7:47.
'less groups': the hands split the Blitzes into groups named A to B2, with 17 instructs 6:30-9:15 re-joining them.
Bombers struck at 11:15 with no anti-air standing (first Nettle 11:48, 1,495 lost); his air plant was never scouted.
An extractor in the plant's exit lane held Blitzes and constructors 30 s at a time (6:24, 10:44, 12:39). This is the defect fixed 2026-10-13 (3aabc77).

Three solars, then the plant's first unit a constructor at 1:12, the intent the lesson names; energy was still empty at 1:31 (13/1300), after which the game was metal-bound with energy full from 3:00.
The commander's 7:47 'eat the wrecks at G1' lifted metal income to 49 at 9:00, but the wrecks known at 12:00-14:00 (1,883 to 3,878 metal) were not being worked at the minute marks.
Turret frames competed with the plant under a metal store at 0 (2:37-8:00) before the priority flag existed. Reader's reading.

summary: A realtime 1v1 against u6bkep (lobby skill 30), Armada against Armada on Comet Catcher, won at 19:37 when group_G killed his commander beside his forward plants at C4. The economy decided it: 21 extractors at 8:00 (pool p75 18) and 34 from 16:00, a light turret at each outer spot and one extractor lost all game, against at most 22 of his ever seen. The army took ten minutes to convert that lead: the raid traded evenly at his C1 turret (5:14-6:50), then the body gathered in our half until 9:29 while he put up a forward plant at C4 (seen 7:30) and turned to Stouts and Janus. At D3 our reinforcements reached the grind in pieces, and we lost 9.8k for 7.3k of his from 9:29 to 14:18. His Stout block and commander broke on our turrets at spot_23 by 15:11, the trade turned our way (16:20-19:06: 7.0k lost for 9.6k), and the 40-unit body reached his commander. Nobody said anything in chat beyond our two banners.

root.what: After the raid's even Blitz trade at his C1 turret, the player pulled the body back to hold and gather at spot_1 in our half ('does not go west of spot_1') until it had about six Stouts. We had income 32 and estimated his at half that. Apart from the 8:12 chase, the body stayed in our half until 9:29. In that window he built the C4 forward plant and turned to Stouts and Janus, so our 2-3x economy then met an army of equal weight in the middle for ten minutes. This is my reading. The commander (a model) argued the same at 7:50.

their_play: Armada vehicles all game, and no air. Blitzes came from the start, first seen 2:46 near his plant. He had about 5 extractors at 2:59 (the player's read) and light turrets at his outer spots, rebuilding the one at spot_4 (C1) after we killed it at 5:19. He met our raid at that turret with Blitzes, and the trades were even from 5:14 to 8:45. His forward vehicle plant at C4 (spot_39) was seen at 7:30 with his first Stouts. Beamers (laser turrets) appeared at B8 (8:27), C1 (12:40), C5 (13:46) and C/D7 (15:06), and Janus from 9:57. For ten minutes he held the middle at D3 and C3 with a Stout and Janus block, his commander fighting in it: at 13:07 the party was his commander, 13 Stouts, a Janus and 2 Blitzes. He added two construction turrets at C4 (13:44) and a third vehicle plant at C4 (17:32). His tier 2 was never seen being built; the first signs were a Consul at 16:17, an advanced constructor at 16:25 and a moho at 18:36. By unique id we saw 77 Stouts, 28 Janus and 32 Blitzes, about 27.5k of soldiers, which is a far bigger economy than the 'three to one' the player assumed. He raided little: one extractor of ours died, spot_21 at 13:45 to Stouts. He did not chat.

summary: A realtime 4v2 on Eclipsed: four seats of ours in the north-east (three Armada, one Cortex; Opus 5.5 medium players on Jev 1.13 under an Opus 5.5 high commander) against thebluegecko and u6bkep, both Armada, in the west. Our first soldiers stood near his start by 2:35-3:02 and the side led about 3,600 to 330 seen at 5:00, but the commander's gathering place meet_d5 lay under his D4 Beamer beside his Pawns, the seats arrived one at a time (6:12-7:23), and the body built by transfer at 8:15 walked into the same C4-D6 nest twice more (9:08-9:33, 11:04-13:10), the second time into his first Welders and a Pit Bull. All the while the side's extractors stood at 29-32 from 8:00 to the end (income about 62) and no tier 2 stood until t4's advanced vehicle plant at 17:20, after four failed placements, against his Welders from 11:10 and a moho at 12:35. After 'The lead is gone' (commander, 14:15) his Stout block killed t4's commander (14:52), a forward Pit Bull post at F6 and 15-16 Welders pinned t3's 10k body at H6-H7, and Liche atomic bombers from an air plant never scouted killed two more commanders at 21:28 and 21:35; the record ends at 21:45.

lens.caveats: There is no truth file: his economy, army and tier-2 clocks are floors from what we saw, and the people's own play is inferred from sightings. There is no ledger row, no results.jsonl and no review.md. The result is inferred from the record's end and the commanders' deaths. minutes.py, analyze_match.py, floor.py, raid_ledger.py and wake_read.py read only record-0/strategist-0, so I ran them on per-seat symlink views in the scratchpad (wake_read on seat 0 only). Per-seat armies include transferred units, so the per-seat windows mislead and the side's sums are the reading. 'His half' is measured from each seat's guessed start (B3, or C8 for t4). pro_baseline.py does not apply (not Comet Catcher). The impedance-review.md (2026-10-16) and unfinished-review.md (2026-10-17) in the match directory are model reviews of harness impedance and frames, not of the game. I build on their facts and differ in ranking: they put the cross-seat join first; I put the gathering place in his reach and the three walks into the nest, with the absent tier 2, as the game's root and cost.

summary: Four seats of ours took 50 extractors by 8:00 and led in army seen (about 3 to 1 at 10:14), but the side's metal income stayed at 110-135 from 8:00 to the end, and no seat began tier 2 until 12:46. thebluegecko held the middle with armed extractors and heavy laser towers from about 8:44. label: human-8v8-1
shape: 5v5: our 2 seats + 3 Apex v0.3.0 seats (all five at +50% income) against 5 people
people: Against us: Gabiiiiiii7 (36), apexearth (31; author of Apex, he hosted the three Apex seats on our side while playing against us), SSFA (17), drakcore (11), [Crd]TimmyT (8). Spectators: computer_whisperer (the user, hosting) and Permisssion. In play the five were Armada, Cortex and two Legion, the Legion in the north-east F1-H2 (the start script lists all five as Armada).
our_side: South box (z 6,554-8,192). t5 Legion at D8 (record-0, bright red 'Yeba') and t9 Cortex at F7 (record-4, dark red 'Nightmare'), lobby side Random, handicap 50 (+50% income). Each seat had an Opus 5.5 medium player, under one Opus 5.5 high commander (68 turns, 46 directions, 6 chat lines). Hands: the pianist on Jev 1.14.0. Allies: three Apex v0.3.0 seats, also at +50%.
summary: A ranked 5v5 on Altored Divide: our Legion (t5) and Cortex (t9) seats and three Apex seats, all at +50%, in the south against five people (rated 36 to 8) in the north, two of them playing Legion in the north-east. Both our seats opened as if at +0, held 8-15 extractors with 8-10 constructors and reached tier 2 late (t5 at 14:27, killed 16:53; t9 at 20:10; the Apex ally at 5:20), so the side fought with tier-1 masses: raids died under the B4 turrets and t9's Thugs trickled into a Legion Incinerator at G2 (its army fell from 14.2k to 6.9k between 13:00 and 18:00), while the trade stayed about even until 27:00. From 25:38 t5's Thanatos, screened by Karkinos, broke the west and the centre (the Armada commander at 35:09, 55k of D1 economy at 35:25), and the people's morale broke with them (32:48: 'there is no units at all on our team'; a resign vote at 36:31). The Legion north-east then held for twenty minutes behind jammed Bastions, hidden from our radar by a ridge, with Tyrannus gunships and an Astraeus behind them: t5's army fell from 108k to 32k at E1/E2 between 45:35 and 47:38 with nothing of theirs seen dying, and t9 piled up 697 Thugs and sent 6-10k commands a minute. The people left one by one from 44:26, and the engine quit at 57:38 with both our commanders alive.

root.what: This is the earliest minute the short win was lost. t9 had 6 extractors and 11 constructors, and the Apex allies held the spots nearby. It stopped making constructors, put the spare ones on wind and reclaim, and switched both labs to Grunts and Thugs. No seat made the tier-2 sprint that a spot-capped team game asks for, and the commander never called for one. The user's reading after the game (commit 9667cfd): 'properly going t2 is a sprint ... in a larger map with allies the gap can be covered'. As a result the side's advanced labs stood at 14:27 (t5, killed 16:53) and 20:10 (t9); the Apex ally's stood at 5:20. t9 never finished a fusion (its first was begun at 57:13). Both seats stayed at 10-11 extractors with income of 109-191 to the end, even at +50%. Everything later is the cost of that minute: tier-1 bodies fed into his tier 2 at G2, then 697 Thugs and blind tier-1/2 masses against a tier-2/3 fortress, which made a 57-minute game out of a game won at 37:00.
root.evidence: t9 note 4:30: 'stuck on 6 extractors with 9 constructors. No more constructors for now ... The labs are switching to Thugs plus Grunts'; report 4:56 'extractors 6 constructors 11'; record-4: coralab created 18:58, finished 20:10; corfus created 57:13.

their_play: Five people of mixed strength, playing mostly as separate bases. The Armada players walked their commanders forward with turrets: B4/A5 nests (an HLT, Beamers, LLTs) and the D3 nest (Beamers, later an Annihilator and a Pulsar). Those posts killed our short-ranged raiders 5:00-10:43. The Armada advanced bot lab at D2 was seen going up at 12:15. A Legion Incinerator at G2/H3 (13:00-18:00) and Cortex gunships from 14:07 punished our tier-1 bodies. An Armada Fatboy/Fido block in the west, 23:00-30:00, fell to t5's Thanatos. The people built fusions and advanced fusions; 55k of that economy at D1 died at 35:25. The decisive player was the Legion north-east, which turtled from 27:00. Its fortress grew to 13+ Bastions (reach 1,100) at E1-H2, with Soteria shields, Erebus jammers, Tyrannus gunships from about 39:30, a rail tank, an Astraeus (reach 3,100), an Experimental Gantry, two Sol Invictus by 56:00, and a nuke silo at H2 that fired once (48:26). It held from 37:00 to 57:00. The people's own words: drakcore 9:50-10:06 'help would be nice ... people just ignore'; Gabiiiiiii7 32:27 'soo late this is not eco game'; [Crd]TimmyT 38:13 'I shoulda built artillery'; apexearth 49:59 'thing is mass bastions does hold off enemies pretty well'. They left one by one from 44:26.

summary: A 2v1 on an island map (sea in columns C-E) against thebluegecko (Cortex, base at A4). On the commander's first direction t1 opened a Hovercraft Platform (1:45) and its Goons were in his box at 3:46; by 9:00 they had killed 15 of his extractors and 7 constructors, while t2 Armada took the south land and water spots and sprinted to an advanced vehicle plant (standing 7:10). summary: A 1v1 on Cape Violet against the user himself at +100% income. We played Cortex in the east and only ever built on land: 3 extractors until 3:00, then 16-19 from 8:00 to the end on 21 distinct spots, while none of the 14 under-water spots east of the middle was ever built (our commander could have built them from 0:00). Our early Incisors reached C5 by 6:38, then went into his Centurions a few at a time at D4-D5 (7:06-7:40), and after that our mass never stood in his half again. His bot wave broke on our turrets and Pounders at F6 (8:33-9:48, 6,458 of his for 2,510 of ours) and we built tier 2 at 9:43, but from 11:59 he took the sea, raised our wrecks with resurrection bots, and went through Fatboys (15:13), a fleet that broke our 16:50 push on the E4 shore, and Titans (23:55). We broke his Fatboy waves at G6 (19-23 min) but lost 11k for 2.4k charging two Titans at F6 (26:47-27:46) and about 27 bombers to their anti-air; an Epoch (29:56) and two nuclear missiles (31:02 and 32:20, no anti-nuke ever finished) ended it, and his base was never seen.

root.what: The player put off the under-water spots and never came back to them. Neither it nor the commander agent ordered a sea extractor, Muskrat, hover constructor or shipyard. Our count stopped at the land ceiling, though 14 spots no bot of ours could walk to lay east of the middle, the nearest (spot_57, G7) 1,175 from home and in reach of the amphibious commander from the first minute.

bears_on.note: Our extractor count was flat at 16-19 from 8:00 to the end, on 21 distinct land spots, with 14 water spots east of the middle never built. The user's post-game reading names expansion as the fault.
The visible killers were Titans, the Epoch and two missiles, but the person's reading puts the loss on extractors (the water slots) twenty minutes earlier.
7:06-7:40: groups B, F and E reached four Centurions one at a time at D4-D5 (#1: 600 lost for 0).
After his wave broke at 9:48, and through the minutes at 3.6x (12:00-13:00) and 2.2-14.6x (17:00-19:00), the body stayed at F6-G6. Those ratios are against the army we saw, which is a floor.

Our Rascals crossed at 3:03 and twelve Incisors at 4:43-6:08, and one extractor of his at C3 died by 4:01. The Incisors were then fed into Centurions. Crossing early is not the same as paying.

lens.caveats: There is no truth file, so all of his numbers are sightings (floors) and minutes.py's ratios compare our army with the army we saw. pro_baseline.py was not run (it covers Comet only; no Cape Violet pool). commander_turns.py and wake_read.py need the 00 directory: on the match directory commander_turns printed nothing. The record's unit_defs 'id' is 1-based, so killers must be named by list index (by id the Titan reads as armawac). There is no ledger row for this game. Where I differ from the existing review: (a) its '39 extractors on land' counts completions (26 cormex + 13 cormoho) on 21 distinct spots; (b) its spot_12 F2 is unwalkable, not a land spot left untaken; (c) it gives 13 water spots in our half, while I count 14 unwalkable spots east of x=5120. I keep its 0:10 root on the user's post-game words; minutes.py alone gives 7:00.

open_questions: Would the 14 east-side water spots (about +13 extractors by 10:00) have held the economy against +100% income? We have no truth file for his extractors; the commander agent's predicts ranged from 13 to 22.

Does a nuclear strike reach the player's report as a missile? The wake called it shelling by 'armsilo (a turret)', and the commander agent misattributed the 31:02 losses.
The brief's Cape Violet plan named Armada's Beaver (armbeaver) while we drew Cortex. The player translated it to a Muskrat, but the sheet's plan is tied to one faction.

summary: Four Opus 5.5 seats under an Opus 5.5 high commander lost at 21:48 on Gecko Isle to three gecko-clan people, the last commander (t5's) dying under a Tzar. The tier-1 game was even to about 10:00 and then ours: the side held 38-39 extractors from 8:00, won the G6 fight at 10:20-11:20, and the commander logged 12.8k of army against about 4.6k seen at 12:50; our advanced vehicle plant had stood since 9:35 on t4, the sprint seat, which held 6 extractors and 14.5 metal a second. The side kept making tier 1 (about 110 soldiers in minutes 10-15, 88 Thugs on t3 over the game) while the advanced constructors' mohos waited on empty stores (3 mohos at 14:00), and the lead sat in our half until 12:50, when all three bodies were sent north after his advanced constructor had been seen (12:20). Nobody, the user included, said anything in the chat; every cause below is the reader's reading.

our_side: Four seats in the east box: t2 Cortex H7 (seat 0), t3 Armada H1 (seat 1), t4 Cortex G4/G5 forward (seat 2), t5 Cortex H5 the tier-2 sprint seat (seat 3); Opus 5.5 medium players under an Opus 5.5 high side commander; hands Jev 1.14.0; lobby names MonkeyLord, obliterator, Amojini, [D]4RK_HUNT[E]R
summary: Our four seats held more tier-1 extractors (27 to 19 at 7:00) and 1.6-8.5x the two people's army from 2:00 to 13:00 (2.2-2.3x at 8:00-10:00, the sum of our four records against the replay's truth), and lost at about 21:05 on the tier-2 economy. The commander's plan (one sprint seat fed by the other three) was sound, but the sprint was fed as surplus: t5 placed its advanced vehicle plant at 4:15 on 9 metal a second, received 450 metal in nineteen minutes and had it standing at 7:39 (3:24 against thebluegecko's 1:46); its advanced constructors went out one at a time, the second idled three minutes on the Armada seat (a harness fault), and the side had 1 moho at 12:00 against their 8. The people sprinted as one team from 7:08 (one advanced bot lab, constructors shared across factions, mohos in 19-33 s with helpers, each advanced plant eaten for the next) while thebluegecko's commander crept heavy turrets into our north at E1-E2 from 6:24, took t3's outer spots and later put his forward advanced plant, two fusions and a Beamer-and-Sheldon nest there. Our army lead was spent in separate bodies, t2 trading at D7 and C6 in the south and t3 losing about 7,700 metal for about 200 in four attacks on the F2-F3 nest (13:11-16:06), and it flipped at 15:00 (7,460 against 10,285); from 17:00 Stouts, Tzars, Sheldons, a Negotiator and Wasps on about four times our income overran t4, t3 and t5 in turn.

root.what: The tier-2 sprint was starved from the minute it was placed. t5 put its advanced vehicle plant down at 4:15 on 4 extractors (9.4 metal a second) while the three feeding seats spent everything on tanks (stores at 0-50) and were asked only for surplus ('every 150 metal that builds up', 0:20 and 4:50). 450 metal reached t5 before 19:32, the plant stood at 7:39, and the moho race was lost 1 to 8 by 12:00. The person's reading (the user) and the commander's own post-mortem point here; the army-lead reading is a turning point below.

summary: A realtime 3v2 on Gasbag Grabens: three Opus 5.5 medium seats (t2 Armada G5, t3 Cortex G3, t4 Armada G2) under an Opus 5.5 high commander against thebluegecko and u6bkep. The commander's plan at 0:02 was a tier-2 sprint at t4 fed by the other two. t4 placed its advanced bot lab at F3 at 3:40, as all eleven of our first raiders were dying at D5-D6 to his larger group, and the feeders' labs paused while the frame took 2:21 (it stood at 6:01) because the feeds moved nothing. Meanwhile his Grunts took all six of t4's extractors (6:13-7:14), u6bkep's commander built a forward bot lab and Beamer at F7 in our half (5:49) that we never struck, and the side never held more than 16 of its 24 spots. From 8:00 u6bkep's Mace and Pawn block razed t2's home and then t3's (t3's commander died at 9:56 and its blast took the base) while t3's body of about 20 walked between G3 and F3, and 21 Grunts killed the advanced lab at 9:17 before its first moho stood. thebluegecko's tier 2 (an Arbiter at 12:38) and a forward nest at F2-F3 (Arbiters, a Sheldon, a Scorpion, a Persecutor) out-ranged t4's last base, and the commander surrendered at about 16:28.

root.what: The side went for the tier-2 sprint at t4 with no cover. The advanced bot lab was placed at F3, 800 west of t4's start and toward the Grunts' E3 path, the minute the first raid had failed in the middle. The commander paused t2's and t3's labs and had t4 eat its tier-1 lab. For the 2:21 the frame took, no seat grew an army or guarded t4's spots, and his forward base at F7 went unanswered. The plant made four advanced constructors and a Welder, then died at 9:17, before its first moho stood (10:22). Our commander's end note and our player's resign line say the same; these are model words, and no person commented.

bears_on.id: The tier-2 sprint: trigger, conduct, feeding, the team procedure, tier 1 against tier 2 and 3
bears_on.note: First test of the team procedure against people (a design test episode, E-sd129-2v3). Conduct worked: plant standing in 1:50 on 3,150 metal of standing transfers. But 'with allies beside you the gap is covered' failed here: a 3v2 on a large map with paused feeders and raiders sent away was not covered, and the clock trigger ignored the brief's 'first bank or spots taken'.
'one constructor and then tanks': our advanced plant made four constructors before its first Bull (9:28), and the side's army stayed below what was raiding it. Infern8 is a less experienced player.

A scope limit: the first handful crossed at 2:00-4:20 in a 3v2 with 9,000-12,000 walks and died to his post, armed extractors and Rascals (about 1,900 for 800), leaving nothing at home. The lesson was given for duels whose first soldiers killed nothing.
Reversed: here the people raided our naked outer extractors (t3's four at 4:21-4:54, 49 side-wide), and our answer was one Blitz or none.
The side took the spots (41 at 10:00) but did not hold them: 41 to 9 by 14:00 under tier-1 raids. Holding needs the army where the spots are.

The extractor collapse (10:00-14:00) came minutes before the end; the loss was on extractors and buildings (16,732 lost) not on the army trade (5,736 of soldiers lost against 9,759 of his destroyed, per the commander's traded line in the ledger).
t3 built four converters at 8:25-9:36 on 'metal-bound, not energy' and they drained 280 e/s from the mohos until 11:29.
'less groups': t2's and t3's bodies never fought together; the Bulls split into four groups by ladder hunts at 13:00-13:20; the people's parties were met one at a time.

The brief's team procedure idles the feeders' plants (t4 87 s, t2 51 s) exactly when his raids arrived; t4's plant then stood dead 9:22-11:00 with a full store. The lesson and the procedure pull opposite ways.

What we built told them what was safe: a side of constructors and mohos with few soldiers met 41 Brutes, 40 Blitzes and 28 Stouts and no tier 2 from them. His own word was that Brutes 'apply more pressure'.
'too many construction bots, made and kept out on the map': side builders 24-29 from 8:00 against 30-36 soldiers (team_read).
